turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. You can drop the jacket on the chair. I just need a couple numbers before Dr. Shah comes in.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, sure. Parking was a mess. Horns the whole time, I can't hear myself think out there.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He griped the entire drive. I'm Linda, his wife. I pretty much hauled him in.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 138 over 82. Heart rate 76. Oxygen 96 percent on room air. Weight 178 pounds.
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Is 138 bad? I don't know, doctor. Oh. You're the nurse. Sorry.
[SEG0006] person_1 (NURSE): Right. Those get passed along. He'll be in in a minute.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hi, I'm Dr. Shah. What brings you in today?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): It's this cough. Every morning I hack up this brown stuff, and there's a frog in my throat till I clear it.
[SEG0009] person_4 (DOCTOR): Morning cough with brown phlegm, throat's gunky until you clear it. How long has that been going on?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Years, I guess. I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0011] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Years. Every single morning. It started long before he quit.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): So it's long-standing, years rather than weeks, and the exact start is unclear. Any chest pain with it?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): The phlegm's like coffee, brown, worse before breakfast. I don't know.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): I'll get the phlegm in a second. Any pain in the chest?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): What about getting short of breath?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): The stairs get me. Halfway up I feel like I've overdone it. And by the afternoon I feel like a wet rag.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Tell him about your feet, hon.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh yeah. My feet feel dead if I sit too long. I don't know, doctor, maybe it's nothing.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Breathless on the stairs, tired by afternoon, feet go numb after sitting. Any fever, or blood in the phlegm?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. And it's brown, not red. I don't see blood.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Has your weight changed?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. Linda does the scale.
[SEG0024] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): It's been stable. Same belt hole for ages.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. Stable, I guess.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Are you still smoking?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, I quit last year. Before that, um, about a pack a day for forty years. I overdid the cigarettes, I know.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): New Year's, last year. He really did stop.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Former smoker, quit last year, about a pack a day for forty years. What medicines do you take?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): The purple inhaler, morning and night. And uh a water tablet for my blood pressure. I think it's twenty five milligrams.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): The purple inhaler, is that Advair, fluticasone with salmeterol?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, Advare. One puff twice a day. The water pill is every morning. I've been on it for the pressure for years.
[SEG0033] person_4 (DOCTOR): Let me have a listen. Some wheeze on the right side, no crackles. Heart sounds are regular.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Is that wheeze a bad thing? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0035] person_4 (DOCTOR): My working impression is chronic bronchitis from all those smoking years. That's provisional. I'm not calling it COPD until the breathing test.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. You're the one who knows this stuff.

[SEG0037] person_4 (DOCTOR): We'll book spirometry. I'd like you to get the pneumonia vaccine and a flu shot if you're not current, and stay off the cigarettes. Come back in four weeks with the results.
[SEG0038] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I'll get him there. Otherwise he'll forget.

spec.situation: Former smoker who quit last year with a long-standing morning cough and brown phlegm; weight stable; no chest pain; spirometry planned; vaccination advice.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.
